cases.pins: Law 1: the surface 通り is itself a dictionary word (the street) and resolves as that word, never via the verb headword 通る the segmenter attached.
The everyday reading stands; the formal わたくし never appears for a plain narrative 私.
Law 2: a chopped stem is displayed in dictionary form (並ぶ), never as the fragment 並ん.
Law 2: 買っ displays as 買う.
Law 4: 今日は stays one entry with the reading the passage's own ruby carries (こんにちは); no 今日/きょう entry may appear beside it.
Law 2: a stem standing before て resolves as its verb and displays in dictionary form.
Law 3: a word no source knows produces NO entry. A missing reading is honest; a guessed one is a defect.
One entry per word shown, in first-appearance order, however often the word recurs.
cases.source: kanjiReadings contract (order of first appearance, deduped by the word shown)

cases.pins: Kana-only surfaces never enter the readings list; the list is a kanji aid, nothing else.
cases.source: kanjiReadings contract (a token qualifies only when its surface carries kanji)

glossStubNote: readingOf below models the deck gloss: the reading of the dictionary entry for the word asked. The 2026-11-11 failures are pinned as cases where the surface and the headword disagree, so the display law, not the stub, decides the entry.
law: Resolution law (2026-11-11, Landry's accuracy flag on the shopping-street card, readerFit.js kanjiReadings): 1) a surface that is itself a dictionary word resolves as THAT word; 2) anything else resolves by headword and is DISPLAYED in its dictionary form; 3) a word no source knows shows NO reading, never a guessed one; 4) the list never contradicts the passage's own ruby.
seededFrom: Landry's hand audit of the N2 'shopping street' morning card, 2026-11-11: 通り listed as とおる (verb) instead of とおり (street); 私 as わたくし instead of わたし; chopped stems 並ん・買っ printed as words; the list contradicting the ruby's 今日は/こんにちは with 今日/きょう.
